claims.claim: Cai uses a random 3:1 theoretical split, ten-fold LASSO selection and a subsequent Cox model, and reports R 3.6.1.
Cai includes 12940 participants and 201 events, with 154/47 events in development/internal validation and overall median follow-up 2016 days.

location.section: Characteristics of the Derivation and Validation Cohorts

claims.claim: Cai's Figure 2 caption combines partial likelihood deviance and binomial deviance wording; Results refers to 18 indicators while the caption describes 19 features.
Cai Table 2 presents LASSO coefficients and lambda.1se, whereas final Cox effects are presented separately as hazard ratios.

location.section: Multivariate Cox Regression Analysis in the Training Cohort

claims.claim: Cai reports DCA using the whole cohort and Hosmer-Lemeshow assessment of calibration.

location.section: Statistical Analyses; Clinical Usefulness of the Predicting Nomogram

claims.claim: Cai reports internal-validation C-index 0.837 and five-year AUC 0.829; these are same-cohort internal results.

location.section: Model Performance for Derivation and Validation Cohort

claims.claim: Han includes 26018 participants, 2640 events, median follow-up 3.05 years and training/validation sizes 12947/13071.
Han selects baseline FPG-defined prediabetes at 5.6-6.9 mmol/L and defines incident diabetes through FPG at least 7.0 mmol/L or self-report.
Han reports missingness of 40.70% for HDL-C, 56.53% for AST and 66.28% each for smoking/alcohol, and describes multiple imputation using linear regression and ten iterations.
Han follows LASSO with full Cox, AIC step-down and MFP comparisons, then derives a seven-predictor continuous model and a categorized score.

location.section: 2.5 Statistical analysis; 3.4 Identification of risk factors

claims.claim: Han prints final continuous-model coefficients and five-year baseline survival in its risk equation.
Han's Supporting information lists an Appendix S1 Excel workbook and time-dependent ROC, calibration and DCA figures.
Liu reports 112070/15453 participants and 1425/373 all-follow-up events in RICH/NAGALA, with only 478/101 events within three years.
Liu describes Efron ties, center-clustered robust standard errors, Schoenfeld assessment, IPCW AUC/Brier and transport of frozen parameters to NAGALA.
Liu uses bootstrap optimism correction and leave-one-center-out validation, and labels matched-spline/time-varying RICH results apparent and DCA exploratory.
Liu examines selection related to missing HDL-C in its complete-case sample and repeats TyG comparisons in expanded samples.
